constraints: RULING FIRST, VERBATIM, in HANDOVER.md and the notebook, before the code in commit order.

RULING D39, COMMITTED VERBATIM: 'Ruling D39 (advisor, 2026-09-30) — one settings map for every path that runs a workflow. Every loop bound a shipped workflow names by setting is resolved from a single function shared by the API path and the eval CLI; no path keeps its own hand-written copy. Rationale: two hand-kept maps drifted. The eval CLI's carries review_rework_attempts and the API path's does not, so the API path ends any blocking review with a ConditionError (reported and reproduced in ARCH-20260930-095's response), while the eval path runs the designed rework loop. The configured bound is the design; a crash is not a conclusion the harness was built to reach. Falsifier: a shipped workflow that names a setting the shared map does not carry. A guard enumerates them.'

ONE SOURCE: a single function, in autornd/config.py beside the settings it reads, returns the lookup. engine/workflow.py and evals/cli.py both call it, and both hand copies are deleted after a reference check recorded in the response (convention 19).

GUARD (free, deterministic): load every workflows/*.yaml through graph.spec.load and assert that every loop whose max_iterations is a string names a key in the shared map. Enumerate from the loaded specs, not by regex. Assert the set of workflows checked is non-empty (convention 28).

API-PATH TEST (convention 22): drive WorkflowEngine (engine/workflow.py) through engineering-rnd with the billing mock client and a review that blocks once. Assert review_rework_loop runs, the status is not a ConditionError, and the configured review_rework_attempts bounds it. PROVE BY BREAKING: remove review_rework_attempts from the shared map and show the guard name review_rework_loop in engineering-rnd. Quote it.
No setting value changes. No workflow change. Free.
